"pull-1098" (2026-08-08T18:46:27Z) — 5 section(s):

[1] "pull-1098" section 1:
Pull request #1098 in re-cinq/lore: feat(skills): add /lore-help, and make every skill document itself
State: merged
Author: gedaiu
Opened: 2026-08-08T14:13:38Z
Closed: 2026-08-08T18:46:23Z
Merged: 2026-08-08T18:46:23Z
Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/lore/pull/1098

Lore ships seven skills and 30+ MCP tools with no index. A developer sees a wall of slash commands and cannot tell which one fits the job in front of them, and nothing in the terminal explains what Lore is or where it helps — the guides that do exist (`docs/using-lore/*.md`, `docs/mcp-tools.md`) live outside the session, so they are read at onboarding and never again.

## `/lore-help`

Three modes:

[2] "pull-1098" section 2:
## `/lore-help`

- **no argument** — what Lore is (three sentences), how a session works (the enforced `lore_assemble_context` → `lore_search_memory` → work → `lore_write_memory` loop), a table of every installed skill, an "I want to…" task router, the four MCP tool families, and links to the deeper guides.
- **`/lore-help lore-pr`** — that skill's documentation, verbatim.
- **`/lore-help "how do I hand this to an agent?"`** — routes to the best match with a one-line reason.

The router answers with **tools as well as skills**, because most Lore capability is not a slash command: delegating is `lore_create_pipeline_task`, recalling a decision is `lore_search_memory`. That is the actual answer to "too many skills".

[3] "pull-1098" section 3:
## The skills document themselves

`/lore-help` writes none of the per-skill docs. Every `SKILL.md` now ends with a `## Help` block — required `**Summary.**` + `**Usage:**`, plus `Use when` / `Not for` / `Examples` / `Related` — fenced by `<!-- lore-help:begin -->` / `<!-- lore-help:end -->`, and `/lore-help` extracts it verbatim. One skill owns its own documentation; there is no second copy to drift. A skill with no block degrades to its frontmatter description with a note saying so — the skill is explicitly forbidden from paraphrasing a skill's instructions into docs or inventing an example.

`scripts/check-skill-help.sh` enforces presence and shape as a new `skill-help` PR check, so a future skill cannot ship invisible to the index. Markers are matched **anchored to the start of a line** — `lore-help`'s own instructions mention them mid-sentence, and an unanchored match swallows that prose (it did, on the first run).

## Closing the trap that would have made this lie

`install.sh` **skipped** any skill directory that already existed, so a skill edited upstream never reached a machine that had installed once — `/lore-help` would have documented behaviour the installed copy did not have. Three changes:

[4] "pull-1098" section 4:
## Closing the trap that would have made this lie

- `install.sh` refreshes a changed skill (`Installed` / `Up to date` / `Updated`) instead of skipping it. These are Lore-owned vendored files; the `Updated` line is the notice that a hand-edit was replaced.
- `lore-doctor` fails its skills check when any shipped skill is absent from `~/.claude/skills` **or differs** from the checkout.
- `/lore-help` reports the same drift in a health footer, and only when there is something to report.

Not theoretical: run today, the check already finds one stale skill (`lore-feature`) on a developer machine.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/check-skill-help.sh` — passes on all seven skills; proven to fail on a removed block and on a malformed one (both exercised against scratch copies).
- The install logic exercised end to end in a temp `HOME`: `Installed` → `Up to date` → `Updated` after an upstream edit.
- The skill's own gather commands run against this machine: drift detection and block extraction both work, including on `lore-help` itself (11 lines, not the whole instruction file).
- `npx eslint .` clean repo-wide; `specs/lore-help/spec.md` is `Draft`, warnings only.

[5] "pull-1098" section 5:
## Verification

No new MCP tool, API route, or DB change. `seed-content.sh` and `lore-ingest.yml` already glob `.claude/skills/**`, so the new skill is ingested with no wiring.

Every `SKILL.md` now ends with a `## Help` block — required `**Summary.**` + `**Usage:**`, plus `Use when` / `Not for` / `Examples` / `Related` — fenced by `<!-- lore-help:begin -->` / `<!-- lore-help:end -->`, and `/lore-help` extracts it verbatim. One skill owns its own documentation; there is no second copy to drift. A skill with no block degrades to its frontmatter description with a note saying so — the skill is explicitly forbidden from paraphrasing a skill's instructions into docs or inventing an example.

`scripts/check-skill-help.sh` enforces presence and shape as a new `skill-help` PR check, so a future skill cannot ship invisible to the index. Markers are matched **anchored to the start of a line** — `lore-help`'s own instructions mention them mid-sentence, and an unanchored match swallows that prose (it did, on the first run).

## Closing the trap that would have made this lie

`install.sh` **skipped** any skill directory that already existed, so a skill edited upstream never reached a machine that had installed once — `/lore-help` would have documented behaviour the installed copy did not have. Three changes:

[4] "pull-1098" section 4:
## Closing the trap that would have made this lie

- `install.sh` refreshes a changed skill (`Installed` / `Up to date` / `Updated`) instead of skipping it. These are Lore-owned vendored files; the `Updated` line is the notice that a hand-edit was replaced.
- `lore-doctor` fails its skills check when any shipped skill is absent from `~/.claude/skills` **or differs** from the checkout.
- `/lore-help` reports the same drift in a health footer, and only when there is something to report.

Not theoretical: run today, the check already finds one stale skill (`lore-feature`) on a developer machine.
